title: From sectoral selection to scientific expertise: A three-tier model for the verification of social practices
abstract: Context and relevance. A significant body of social practices has been accumulated in the field of childhood, identified through competitions, monitoring, and other sectoral procedures; however, such selection does not ensure the assessment of their evidence base or independent scientific verification. The persistent gap between accumulated practical experience and the scientific substantiation of the effectiveness of social interventions necessitates building a verification system that guides a practice from initial selection to evidence-base assessment and scientific expertise. Objective. Theoretical and methodological justification for a three-stage model of verification of social practices in the field of childhood, including sectoral selection, basic verification, and independent scientific expertise. Results. It is shown that the three-tier model bridges the gap that has emerged in the domestic social sphere between accumulated practical experience and the scientific substantiation of the effectiveness of interventions, and makes it possible to differentiate the responsibility of network participants: sectoral agencies and competition platforms, developers of practices, and the expert and academic community. The logic of a practice's progression between levels is examined: from a “candidate technology”, through description in accordance with uniform requirements, to the status of a practice with proven effectiveness and its inclusion in federal registries. The principles of applying the evidence-based approach in the practice of childhood professionals are described, making it possible to combine the rigor of the evidence-based paradigm with the flexibility needed to take into account the specifics of particular types of practices and the stages of their life cycle. Conclusions. The proposed model sets out the general logic of verifying social practices, linking sectoral selection, assessment of the evidence base, and independent scientific expertise, and making it possible to delineate the functions of the participants in this process. Further elaboration is required for the procedures of verifying international practices and for approaches to evaluating practices in those areas of the social sphere where the possibilities of applying experimental research designs are limited.
